title: Holding a role is judged purely formally, so leave of absence, no pay, or alternating shifts are no defence
content:
A.1.5.5 forbids an Alignment Conserver from being operationally active in more than one AC role or other ecosystem role. The Action Tenet at A.1.5.5.0.4.1 then removes every plausible way to argue around it: "As long as an entity occupies or assumes a role that is formally defined in the Atlas, that entity is 'operationally active' in that role. This is notwithstanding the amount of time the entity devotes to a role; the nature of the work performed... the fact that the entity is on a leave of absence from one role; the fact that the entity's role is uncompensated; or the fact that the entity alternates between two roles to avoid simultaneous performance of both roles."

The rationale is explicitly about *information and incentives*, not workload: the risk arises "when a stakeholder occupies two or more ecosystem roles, each of which has different mandates and inner incentives," producing "conflict of interest and bias, collusion and conspiracy."

That is why a formal test is the correct one here. Substantive tests — did the second role actually influence the first? — require proving a counterfactual about someone's reasoning, which is unprovable and therefore unenforceable. Formal occupancy is observable. The scenarios show the enforcement in action: alternating between AD and Facilitator in separate time intervals is Misaligned because "they still have access to sensitive information and experiences in two roles with different mandates and incentives" (A.1.5.5.0.4.1.1.1), and even an *on-call* second role fails, because "it is conceivable that Entity's decision-making in their first role could be compromised or influenced, even in subtle ways" (A.1.5.5.0.4.1.1.2).

The accepted cost is over-inclusion: entities are removed for arrangements that may have caused no harm at all. The framework takes that trade because the alternative is a rule that only bites when harm is already proven.
description: A.1.5.5.0.4.1 makes occupancy of an Atlas-defined role sufficient regardless of hours, nature of work, compensation, or absence — a bright-line test chosen over substantive assessment.
